findings.title: Action and its formed path
findings.claim: The focus links each person's shakilah to action and then to a path on which guidance is assessed. The surrounding pericope makes that relation lived: 17:83 shows reactions under favor and adversity; 17:90-93 show actors setting conditions for what they will accept; 17:94-95 fit a messenger's form to the recipients imagined before it; and 17:96 places the appraisal within divine witness. The personal way can therefore be heard as a course that shapes and constrains action, whose direction becomes perceptible in the path.
findings.mechanism: Shakilah is the carrier of a personal way; ya'malu supplies the action that proceeds through it, while ahda and sabil name guidance and its path-domain. The native context supplies independent cases of response, self-set acceptance conditions, matched delivery, and witnessed conduct. The same-root fetter image contacts the conditional demands by analogy: like a tether, they restrict what the actors will let through.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's manner is no longer only an inward label. The pericope lets the reader see conduct as its output and a path as the direction in which that conduct becomes assessable.
findings.containment: This does not make the path predetermined or claim that all the surrounding scenes share one cause. The fetter is analogical, 17:90-93 may be tactical bargaining, 17:94-95 directly answers a particular objection, and the primary reading remains that each person acts according to a personal way while the Lord knows best who is more guided.

epistemic.reason: The channel nomination is trusted and every focus branch has a registered facet; its macro synthesis uses exact pericope surfaces, while the cited HFT contextual roles remain legacy-unbound.

findings.title: Revelation held within the Lord's authority and mercy
findings.claim: The focus names the Lord as the knower of paths; the surrounding context gives that title a concrete relation to revealed guidance. The host basmala names Allah as compassionate and merciful, 17:86 says the revelation could be taken away at will, and 17:87 names its preservation as mercy and great favor from the Lord. The comparison of who is better guided thus sits within the authority and mercy by which guidance is made available.
findings.mechanism: The focus Rabb carrier meets the paired context of possible withdrawal and merciful preservation. The basmala and 17:87's Lord-and-mercy phrase reinforce the same local relation, while 17:86 supplies the independent authority trigger.
findings.reader_payoff: Guidance appears not only as a path to assess but as revelation whose availability is held within the Lord's authority and mercy.
findings.containment: The context speaks specifically about revelation to the Messenger; it does not say that every human act is determined or that mercy replaces the focus's account of personal action.

epistemic.reason: The Arabic context directly supplies mercy, possible withdrawal, and the Lord-title; their relation to the focus's knowledge of paths is a writer's macro inference.

findings.title: The assessed path is also requested
findings.claim: In the focus, the Lord knows who is more rightly guided along a path. The added Fātiḥa lines turn that carrier toward the reciter: 1:6 asks to be guided to the straight path, and 1:7 names the path of those who received favor. The reader is therefore not only hearing an assessment of guidance but also voicing a request to enter a path whose human course is described.
findings.mechanism: The focus ahda carrier meets the same guidance root in the imperative ihdina at 1:6; the sabil carrier meets the requested straight path in 1:6 and the path of the favored in 1:7. This direct contact shifts the focus's comparison from detached observation to a question the reciter also inhabits.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees the comparative statement beside a personal and communal request for the very direction under discussion.
findings.containment: This is a local overlay from the individually supplied ayat 1:6-7, not a claim that 17:84 quotes them, that sabil and sirat are lexically identical, or that the focus imports the whole Fātiḥa theme.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches are supplied with trusted nominations and the added ayat give exact guidance/path carriers; the reader-facing relation between assessment and supplication is an inference.
